newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Barrick has examined Great Central -source.
newsitem.headline: Barrick has examined Great Central -source.

text.p: Executives from Canada's Barrick Gold Corp recently examined the operations of Western Australian gold miner Great Central Mines Ltd, an industry source told Reuters.

The source said the executives had now returned to Canada and it was not known if the visit would lead to a takeover bid, which has been widely rumoured in the local share market over the past two days.
Controlled by Melbourne businessman Joseph Gutnick, Great Central is ranked as a major local miner with expected 1997 output of more than 500,000 ounces.
"Barrick was here. They looked at Great Central's assets and that was the only one they looked at in Australia before they went away," said the source.
Great Central told the Australian Stock Exchange earlier on Wednesday that it had not received a takeover offer from Barrick and was not aware of any offer.
Great Central shares were 25 cents higher at A$2.71 at 2.20 p.m. (0420 GMT), valuing the company at A$688.43 million based on 254.03 million shares outstanding.

A Barrick spokesman said from the company's head office in Toronto that he had no comment on the takeover reports which were prominently displayed in the financial pages of most local newspapers on Wednesday.
The Australian Financial Review newspaper said Gutnick was a willing seller of his controlling 24.7 percent stake in Great Central.

Gutnick said Great Central had received a number of overtures from potential bidders in recent weeks, with the focus being on favourable asset valuations in Australia compared with North American counterparts.
